item.title: At 22, Jayden Williams became Stockbridge’s youngest mayor; 10 months later, the city council...
item.description: In a surprising turn of events, Stockbridge's youngest mayor, Jayden Williams, was ousted following a misconduct hearing. The city council uncovered serious concerns surrounding his management of resources and city property. Facing claims of financial impropriety, Williams defended himself by pointing to insufficient training. Now, Stockbridge is preparing for a special election to choose a new mayor to bridge the leadership gap.

item.title: Western Australia created two reefs with 60 concrete boxes; fish species rose from 12 to more than 60
item.description: Launched in 2013, purpose-designed artificial reefs were deployed along Western Australia's coast, leading to a remarkable transformation of the seafloor. In a span of three years, fish species surged from a mere dozen to an impressive sixty. These artificial structures not only enrich marine biodiversity but also provide excellent recreational fishing sites, exemplifying the project's effectiveness in promoting both marine life and community involvement.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 5,800 acres in New York’s Adirondack Park head to auction
item.description: A large Adirondack Park property, planned for extensive residential development, is now headed for a public foreclosure auction. This project, which promised hundreds of homes and a ski resort, faced significant legal challenges. After years of litigation and mortgage defaults, the land's ownership became entangled in foreclosure proceedings. An investor is owed millions, and the county also seeks significant property tax payments.

item.title: Why don't birds fall out of trees while sleeping? The unusual science behind the phenomenon
item.description: Birds have evolved unique adaptations that allow them to sleep safely on tree branches. Special tendon and leg structures automatically secure their feet when their legs bend, which maintains balance even in slightly moving branches. Some birds also utilize their foot shape and balance for perching, while others may choose to rest on one leg to conserve heat during colder weather.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Arizona’s Apache trout neared extinction; after recovery, a new barrier protects 22 miles of habitat
item.description: Arizona's Apache trout has seen a stunning recovery from the brink of extinction, largely due to the proactive conservation efforts spearheaded by the White Mountain Apache Tribe. Officially taken off the list of federally protected species in September 2024, this fish now thrives in its natural habitat, shielded from invasive trout by a newly erected barrier. Ongoing management and monitoring of the species are essential for ensuring its long-term survival.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: US-Mexico river deal cuts Mexico’s Colorado River share by 250,000 acre-feet for 2 years
item.description: Mexico's commitment to draw less water from the Colorado River system showcases a proactive approach amid ongoing sustainability challenges. This two-year agreement, lauded by experts for its exemplary binational collaboration, emerged from a series of meetings held by a dedicated commission. It aims to provide essential water stability for users in Mexico as US states continue to navigate their differing priorities.

item.title: UN warns Ebola may not have peaked in DR Congo, despite falling cases
item.description: The Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo shows early signs of slowing. Daily infections have decreased from approximately 120 to about 80 cases. However, transmission continues to rise in some areas, officials caution. Mobile data tracks population movements to predict future virus spread. Kisangani has emerged as a key area of concern due to its transport hub status.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: Scientists turned rice plants into tiny power sources and reduced methane from paddy fields
item.description: Researchers harnessed rice plants to generate electricity using plant microbial fuel cells. Activated biochar electrodes improved power density and lowered methane emissions significantly. The rice-based system produced higher voltage than sediment-based fuel cells. This technology offers a promising step for sustainable energy generation in paddy fields. Further development is needed for large-scale application of this innovative system.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: RMIT researchers turn cigarette butts into bricks, reducing firing energy use by 10%
item.description: Researchers are developing methods to recycle discarded cigarette butts into lightweight bricks. This innovative approach aims to reduce environmental pollution from cigarette waste. Incorporating butts into bricks can also lower energy requirements during production. The research explores collecting and processing cigarette filters on an industrial scale. This initiative could significantly decrease litter and manufacturing costs globally.

item.title: How Josh Duhamel turned a rustic cabin into a 52-acre retreat
item.description: Actor Josh Duhamel has acquired a tranquil property in Minnesota, initially featuring just an old cabin. Over the years, he expanded the land to fifty-two acres, modernizing it with essential utilities like electricity and running water. This transformation has provided a beloved retreat for his family, where they can enjoy a range of outdoor activities, including leisure time by the lakeside with his son.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: After years of drainage efforts for farming, Wisconsin family’s 2,000 acres are now protected
item.description: A nearly 2,000-acre former farm along Wisconsin’s Sugar River is now permanently protected after years of drainage efforts and a tax dispute. Groundswell Conservancy and Ducks Unlimited bought the property, which includes wetlands, floodplain forests and prairies. The land will become part of the Avon Bottoms Wildlife Area and remain open for hiking, fishing, hunting and wildlife watching.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: This woman spent a night inside the real Conjuring House: “You didn’t feel alone”
item.description: A horror enthusiast recounted her bizarre overnight adventure at the infamous Conjuring House, a nearly 300-year-old farmhouse in Rhode Island that inspired the renowned film series. She described the atmosphere as unsettling and 'sickening,' creating an intense discomfort for anyone inside. With a notorious history of paranormal events, the location fascinates thrill-seekers, though it is currently closed for repairs and public access.
